events.title: One each
events.text: A skiff gutted for parts long ago and then, oddly, tidied. Someone has swept the deck and stacked the cargo box by the hatch, with a note taped to the lid in careful capitals: ONE EACH. THE NEXT ONE WILL BE GRATEFUL.

outcomes.text: One is a fistful of scrap in a freezer bag, tied neatly. You take it. The box seems fuller than before, which cannot be right.

choices.text: Take one and leave one of your own.

outcomes.text: You trade five scrap of your own for the bag and tie the new bag shut with the same knot. Something on the Rusthold channel clears its throat, approvingly.

choices.text: Leave the box for someone who needs it.

outcomes.text: You re-tape the note, which has come a bit unstuck. Somebody will be glad. You are glad, in the end, that it will not be you.

events.title: Embarrassed
events.text: A one-seat Scrapper runabout drifts ahead with its nav lights blinking the long-short that means no emergency, just embarrassed. The pilot has been out of fuel for two hours and has been rehearsing her apology for most of them.

choices.text: Tow her to the nearest light.

outcomes.text: It takes forty minutes and a good deal of her gratitude. She pays what she can and apologises again on the way out, which brings the total to nine apologies.

choices.text: Hand her a can of fuel.

outcomes.text: The can goes across on a line. She kisses it, then looks mortified at having kissed it, then gives you everything in her wallet and a rating of five on the Rusthold board.
You wave. She waves back with the dignity of someone who would have done the same, and then goes back to rehearsing.

events.title: First week
events.text: A Rusthold apprentice on a cargo scooter, a tray strapped across the handlebars: bolts, rounds, a jar of something with a hand-drawn label. She has the look of someone in her first week, and the manner of someone who has been told not to show it.

choices.text: Buy a box of rounds (8 credits).

outcomes.text: She counts out six rounds into a bag, carefully, and then adds a seventh when she thinks you are not looking. You decide not to be looking.
She weighs it on a scale that is not quite level, frowns, and corrects for it in your favour. 'Ma says to be fair,' she says. 'Ma says it a lot.'

choices.text: Ask how the first week is going.

outcomes.text: 'It's all right,' she says. 'Everyone says the first jump is worst, and then you go, and it's just a jump.' She straightens the tray. 'Stay near the lights, that's all I'd say.'

choices.text: Tip two fingers to her cap and go.

outcomes.text: She tips two fingers back, a beat late, and looks surprised at herself.
